# O:I — Responsibility, Source, Projection and Contribution

## Identity and evidence standing

This selected internal technical bundle joins authored positions, product contracts, source/projection architecture and a bounded executable floor. The documents retain their separate identities inside the manifest. The O:I checkout was inspected at committed head `c1ce2db81eec3b03a9bdff0a1accf8ece4acf903`. FOUNDING-POSITIONS.md, OBJECTIVE-CO-INTERNALITY.md and social.mjs matched that commit. CANONICAL-PRODUCT-FIELD.md did **not**: its inspected working bytes include the 2026-09-06 S=CLI / M′=desktop owner clarification. Its working SHA-256 is `bb1cfcf38abf8d16095cdff5af0424aea5f120b695b64e093500523a0a105456`; these bytes must not be attributed to the committed head.

The August capstone contracts retain their dates and original census scope. Their reported read/navigation floor and higher-order authoring gaps are historical statements, not a September software acceptance audit. Later ratification governs present native cardinalities and recursive local Bimba. Full readings are reused from the immutable T21 packet; exact originals and SHA-256 values are retained in the local manifest. No external published edition or direct quotation is claimed.

## Consumption and limits

The [O:I responsibility dossier](../../../../dossiers/oi-technical-responsibility.md) develops the relation between authorisation, source, projection, contribution, encounter and acceptance. A projected account remains distinct from its source; a returned contribution retains attribution and can be accepted, revised, refused or left divergent. These contract operations are not proof of hosted admission, UI completion, learning, authentication or deployment. The six direct checks establish only the listed constructor behaviours.
